# A context a directory package declares is part of what it exports, as a
# library's is: `p.server(v) { … }` provides it, a test sets it with
# `t.setContext(p.server, v)`, and a function of the package reads whichever
# is active. The package's view used to hold every declaration but its
# contexts, so the provider was an unknown component.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out app.sngl
grep 'p_where\(\)|where\(' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import p "./p"
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

component page node {
    var got = "-"
    p.server("mirror") {
        button #ask(text="ask", @click { got = p.where() })
    }
    text(value=got)
}

func testProvided(t Test, c page) {
    c.ask.click()
    t.assert(c.got == "mirror")
}

func testSet(t Test) {
    t.assert(p.where() == "default")
    t.setContext(p.server, "set")
    t.assert(p.where() == "set")
}

window {
    page
}
-- p/p.sngl --
context #server("default")

func where() string {
    return server
}
